\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.LogspaceUniform}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Logspace-uniform circuit family]
\lean{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform}
\label{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable}
A family of Boolean circuits is logspace-uniform if there is an implicitly
logspace-computable function from bit strings to bit strings that, on the string of $n$
true bits, outputs the encoding of the circuit in the family for inputs of length $n$,
for every natural number $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Logspace uniformity implies polynomial-time uniformity]
\lean{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform.isPUniform}
\label{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform.isPUniform}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsPUniform, Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.polyTimeComputable}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic Boolean circuits. If $C$ is logspace-uniform,
then it is polynomial-time-uniform: a polynomial-time-computable function outputs the
encoding of $C_n$ on the unary input of length $n$, for every $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logspace uniformity implies polynomial size]
\lean{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform.isPolySize}
\label{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform.isPolySize}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsLogspaceUniform.isPUniform, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsPUniform.isPolySize, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.IsPolySize}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic Boolean circuits. If $C$ is logspace-uniform,
then there are natural numbers $a$ and $k$ such that $\mathrm{size}(C_n)\leq a(n+1)^k$
for every $n$.
\end{theorem}
